title: Throwing a large casserole lid and knob
subtitle: Measuring, throwing, and fitting a flanged lid for a large casserole pot
excerpt: A casserole lid must fit its pot precisely and carry a knob strong enough to pick it up safely. This technique covers measuring the gallery diameter with calipers before throwing, making the domed lid form upside-down on the wheel, and attaching a pulled or thrown knob at leather-hard.
sourceNotes: Technique synthesised from standard wheel-throwing references and practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stepped ledge thrown inside the rim of a pot onto which a lid rests
The drying stage where clay holds its shape and can be carved or joined with slip
A downward-projecting lip on a lid that fits inside the pot neck to keep the lid stable

content.text: A casserole lid is thrown upside-down so the dome forms naturally from the centred mound. The
is thrown at the outer rim of the lid (the underside when in use) and must match the
diameter of the casserole body. Measure the gallery with calipers before throwing the lid.

materials.name: Smooth stoneware clay (for the lid dome)

content.text: Before throwing the lid, use calipers to measure the inside diameter of the casserole gallery. Keep the calipers set to this measurement throughout. Check the flange diameter against them before trimming.
Fix a bat and centre 450 g of stoneware into a low, wide dome shape. The dome will become the lid's top surface.

Open the base of the dome by pressing down in the centre to a depth of 8 mm (this will become the inside of the lid). Widen the opening to create a shallow dish shape that domes upward at the outer edges.

At the outer rim, pull the wall slightly inward and downward to form the flange. Check the inner diameter of the flange against the calipers: it must match the gallery diameter. Allow 3 to 5% for shrinkage in drying and firing.
Needle-trim the top of the flange level. Smooth the dome surface with the wooden rib. Leave on the bat to firm.
, centre it on the wheel in its correct orientation (dome upward, flange facing down toward the wheel). Use wadding clay to hold it steady.

Score a circle 3 cm in diameter at the top centre of the dome. Apply slip. Form the 80 g knob by throwing or pulling a thick cylinder and shaping its base to 3 cm diameter. Score and slip the base and press firmly onto the lid top.
Blend the base of the knob into the lid surface with a wet finger. Allow to dry slowly before bisque firing.

items.problem: Lid does not sit level in the gallery and rocks
items.cause: The flange diameter was thrown slightly larger or smaller than the gallery, or the flange wall varies in thickness around the circumference
items.fix: At leather-hard, place the lid in the gallery and mark the high points. Trim the flange carefully with the needle tool and wire to even the fit. A slight draught toward the flange inside helps the fit on firing

items.problem: Knob cracks at the base where it meets the lid
items.cause: The knob clay was drier than the lid when attached, causing differential shrinkage
items.fix: Score and slip both the knob base and the lid surface thoroughly. Blend the join with a wet finger. Dry the assembled lid slowly under a loose cloth to equalise drying rates
